title: Gadget guide: What students must know before buying

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Before spending their hard-earned savings on a new tool, student buyers need a reliable gadget guide to help them make informed and confident decisions on their next big purchase.
We’ve created a list of things that students should remember, know, and avoid before deciding on their next gadget purchase that will empower their studies in the coming years.
Where do I start planning?

From drafting research papers to delivering group presentations, a student’s daily routine requires a gadget that strikes the balance between performance, storage, build quality, and the right price. But with so many options on the market, knowing where to start your search can feel overwhelming.

The most common pitfall of student buyers is falling into extremes: They pay extra for high-end features that they seldom use, or they settle for cheaper and underpowered alternatives where they sacrifice the workflow needed to get the job done.

To avoid these mistakes, start by listing the specific software your courses or subjects do require. Identifying whether you primarily use productivity ecosystems or cloud suites like Google Workspace and Microsoft 365, or even heavy specialized software, is an essential first step in narrowing down your search for the next gadget purchase.
And here are some points to take care of when beginning to map out in searching for the next gadget:

items: Identifying your Primary Use Case — Everyone has a different set of needs, and that’s okay. Remember that computer science and multimedia students require a different set of technical specifications and hardware compared to those in education, humanities, or business courses that typically produce essays and presentations. Thus, it is important to determine what your current technology needs are. You might also want to ask yourself: “How will my next gadget benefit my studies in the long term?”
Mobility Check — Are you fine prioritizing raw power and screen space with desktops, or do you opt for portability in usage such as tablets, iPads, or laptops?

Check your current ecosystem — With the current technology that you have, check how it will be compatible with syncing with the new device that you’re planning to buy. In this state, are your existing devices compatible well with the devices you aim for–-like pairing an iPad with a Mac or MacBook? Or pairing an Android tablet with a Windows laptop?

Set a strict budget for the purchase — Allocate your financial resources wisely for your next device, and stick to what’s readily available to you. Don’t settle for less—and we recommend that if your needs require more powerful software for more powerful gear, then you would want to invest more financially.

The big four of gadget spending
When evaluating and canvassing for any gadget purchase, students usually look for these four major factors, ensuring they get the maximum value for their money before deciding on their next purchase:

items: For Laptops/Desktops: You need to focus on the processor (CPU) and memory (RAM). When using for general schoolwork, you might want to look for at least that is a mid-range processor (e.g., Intel Core i5, AMD Ryzen 5, or the Apple M-Series) that’s paired with at least 16GB of RAM for future-proofing. Enough RAM prevents your system from slowing down when you have multiple browser tabs open, a video call, and document editors open at once.

For Phones: You may want to opt for a phone with a mid-range to flagship processor. Aim also for at least 8GB of RAM, as well as a 90Hz or 120Hz display refresh rate that gives users reading long documents and scrolling through lecture slides smoothly.
For Laptops/Desktops: Always go for the Solid State Drive (SSD) over a Hard Disk Drive (HDD). Aim to go for 512GB of internal storage when you can.

For Phones: 128GB of storage is the absolute minimum in the current tech economy, where 256GB is the sweet spot for long-term usage, if you are looking to keep your phone for the next three to five years.

For Laptops/Desktops: You might want to use student discounts outside the tagged price seen in physical stores. If you require software subscriptions or even accessories, you need to count that also towards the price. Standard entry-level laptops can currently range from ₱25,000 to ₱35,000, as the price of computer parts has gone up in recent months.

For Phones: Mid-range or flagship-killer phones can give more features that are close to the top-of-the-line features for half of their price. You might also want to check out back-to-school promos offered with software bundles so you can get more for less.

For Laptops: Ask the retailers if the RAM and the storage are upgradable. This is crucial if you plan to expand the longevity of your laptops in the future. You might want to have a laptop that runs for 8-10 hours without needing to charge, especially if you have long days on campus.

For Phones: 5000mAh battery-powered phones are now typically more affordable in many phones. With this capacity, it already ensures that your phone can go on long days without the need to charge at a wall outlet. Your phone should also have developer support so that it can receive updates for at least 3-5 years. You will also want a durable phone that has scratch-resistant glass and that can withstand daily wear-and-tear and accidental spills.

blocks.text: What to look out for to avoid scams
Student buyers are a common target of scammers, and getting guides on how to safeguard your finances can help you get peace of mind.

items: Buy only through Authorized Sellers — Generally, we recommend visiting a physical store of your choice near you, so you can physically examine the gadget you wish to purchase. And should you have any questions, you can ask the sales representatives directly. However, if the store location is too far from your location, then you should buy from the official distributors or even from flagship stores of major online shopping platforms.

Be Extra Careful When Shopping in Local Marketplaces — When transacting through local marketplaces or online platforms such as Facebook Marketplace, always meet the seller in a secure, public place (like a busy mall or coffee shop) and test the device physically and ensure its full functionality before payment.

Check for Account Locks — If buying a second-hand device, check if the previous owner has wiped all personal data. If you see that the device is locked, it’s basically a bricked device and must be avoided.

blocks.text: Maximize online student discounts
Being a student means living on a tight budget, but your official academic email address is a golden ticket to substantial digital savings.
Before paying full retail price for the apps and media you rely on every day, students can use these discounts to ease the financial burden while boosting productivity and entertainment.

Spotify Premium and YouTube Premium offer a special discount for student subscriptions. Both streaming platforms offer ad-free, uninterrupted playback while doing your study sessions or an intense review for an upcoming quiz or examination.

For other software that is generally free or has cheap subscriptions, you may want to check with your school’s IT Office first about using cloud suites, as most schools provide free, full access by logging in with student credentials.

Additionally, productivity apps like Notion also offer free upgrades to their premium Personal/Plus tiers for users with .edu accounts, which unlock more features such as unlimited file uploads and advanced workspace organization.
Investing in a new gadget as a student isn’t about buying a flashy, top-tier device on the market; it is about finding the right tool for your academic journey.

Just like doing your research, your next gadget purchase should be as careful as you do your thesis: By doing extensive research and considering your needs, requirements, and proper resource allocation without falling victim to scams, you get value for your money’s worth.
